subject: Capacity claims & weighted seating for Atlas Robotics onboarding
messages:
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@atlas-robotics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: purchasing@atlas-robotics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing confirmation (Atlas onboarding)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we discussed on the call, Atlas is planning to cut over a high-throughput inference workload in mid-December and the contract references a dedicated tranche (4 x A100 equiv) for the first 90 days. Procurement needs a written confirmation of the slice and start date so we can finalize internal budgets.

I attached the sizing spec and the draft MAP (minimal actionable plan) for handoff. Quick asks: can you confirm whether the tranche is pinned to our deal ID, whether there is a preemption policy, and whether Redwood can commit to 3 ms p95 latency for our 2048 token baseline?

We are on a tight runway — if we can get written confirmation by end of day Friday, we can meet our December 15 go-live.

Thanks,
Jamie
Jamie Ortiz
Head of Platform
Atlas Robotics

Attachments: atlas_dedicated_sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP_draft.md
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing confirmation (Atlas onboarding)

Jamie —

Thanks for the spec and the heads up. Short answers up front: we can reserve the tranche under ATLAS-2026-Q4 but there are active allocation constraints in the pool for that week. Preemption policy: we do have weighted preemption tiers (enterprise reserved > committed > best-effort). Latency claim for 2048 baseline is plausible on the configured stack but I need ops confirmation on kernel choices and queue depth.

Ben / Marissa — can you validate capacity for the requested 4-GPU equivalent starting 2026-12-15 through 2027-03-15 and call out any conflicts with existing committed deals? If we cannot fully pin, please propose a mitigated seating plan (e.g., weighted seating, percent-of-tranche, or staged ramp).

Jamie — attaching our most recent proposal (proposal_v3.pdf). I'm flagging this as time-sensitive. Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement and ops.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing confirmation (Atlas onboarding)

Karthik / Jamie —

I ran the tranche forecast against the reserve calendar. Short version: the physical GPU pool that would serve a 4x A100-equivalent tranche on 12/15 is 92% utilized the week of 12/13 because of an overlapping BrightBridge onboarding (BrightBridge has a signed reserved contract for 6x, start 12/10). We have three levers here:

1) Ask BrightBridge to shift their start by 7–10 days (high friction — they are revenue critical and already in ramp).
2) Split capacity for the first 90 days using a weighted seating model (e.g., Atlas 60% / BrightBridge 40% of the active tranche), with automatic preemption to enterprise reserved when higher-tier traffic is detected.
3) Offer Atlas a temporary burst pool with higher cost (on-demand GPUs) and a guaranteed ramp path to 4x when next refill window opens (mid-Jan).

Operational constraints I'll call out: KV cache persistence across split seating is non-trivial — if we split a model instance across two customers we will pay an efficiency penalty and see a small latency variance at cold start. Also, our autoscaler cannot enforce percent-of-tranche at the hardware affinity layer today without a manual pin.

Recommendation: if Atlas has contractual SLA / revenue at stake, option 2 with 60/40 for 90 days is the lowest friction that preserves BrightBridge ramp and satisfies Atlas near-term needs. We'll document it as a temporary seating claim, with an ops playbook to migrate Atlas to dedicated pinned capacity in the next quarter.

Ben Carter
Head of Capacity & Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: capacity_heatmap_week50.png (image)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing confirmation (Atlas onboarding) — decision requested

Laura —

Forwarding a short thread. Atlas wants a hard confirmation by EOD Friday to keep their 12/15 go-live. Ops flagged a conflict with BrightBridge (signed reserve starting 12/10). Ben proposes a temporary weighted-seating (Atlas 60% / BrightBridge 40%) for the first 90 days with a documented migration path.

Key commercial considerations:
- Atlas is a new enterprise deal; expected ARR (year 1) is material and procurement will accelerate if we give onboarding certainty.
- BrightBridge is an existing customer mid-ramp; pushing them is high risk to renewal/CSAT.

For the exec ask: do we approve a seating claim that temporarily reduces BrightBridge active capacity share (operationally implemented as a percent-of-tranche split) for 90 days in exchange for Atlas signing a committed reserved capacity starting Q1? Or do we require Atlas to take a burst-on-demand ramp instead?

Quick call fine — otherwise can we get confirmation by 5pm PST?

—Karthik
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing confirmation (Atlas onboarding) — decision requested

Team —

After weighing commercial and operational risk, I approve a temporary weighted-seating claim for Atlas with the following guardrails:

1) Allocation: approve 60% of the contested tranche to Atlas for 90 days (2026-12-15 — 2027-03-15). BrightBridge retains 40%.
2) SLA & cost: Atlas must sign a Q1 reserved commitment (minimum 6-month term) within 14 business days or the seating claim reverts; during the 90-day period Atlas will pay a 10% uplift on the tranche unit price to cover efficiency loss.
3) Ops mitigation: Ben to deliver an ops playbook (step-by-step) to implement percent-of-tranche routing, KV cache warming plan, and a rollback procedure within 48 hours of this decision. Include test checklist for latency p95 verification.
4) Communication: Karthik to send Atlas a formal confirmation email (copy legal and procurement). CC BrightBridge with a short note and an offer for a credit offset for the temporary share reduction.

Ben / Marissa — please attach the capacity_claim_form.xlsx with the exact pinning and monitoring hooks. Karthik — loop in legal for contract amendment language.

I'll monitor the outcome; escalate to me if BrightBridge reports material degradation or if latency targets are missed during the trial.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_claim_form.xlsx (spreadsheet)
